header: THE BROWSER'S CONSOLE, IN A FILE (my request, 22 Nov 2026). While the app runs in DEVELOPMENT, everything the page writes to the browser's console (log, info, warn, error, debug), every uncaught error, every unhandled promise rejection and every picture or script that fails to load is sent to the server, which appends it to `.browser-console.log` in the project folder: the same idea as `.dev-server.log` for the terminal, so I can read the whole picture (terminal AND browser) from two files. The file is started afresh whenever the dev server starts (npm run dev:log empties it; the route empties it at its first write too). Nothing of this exists in production: the layout does not add the script, and the route answers 404. The script is plain text that the root layout puts in <head>, so it is running BEFORE React hydrates: a hydration error is written during hydration, and a script that waits for a component would miss it. It keeps its own copy of the page's `console` methods and calls them first, so the browser's console looks exactly as before. I leave only Next's "[Fast Refresh]" and "[HMR]" lines (reload chatter) out of the file.

doc: I take the entries of a request body, check them and cut them to size; anything that is not an entry is dropped.

symbols.name: formatEntries
doc: I write one line per entry: the time, the level, the page, then the message. A message of several lines keeps its lines, indented, so the next entry is easy to find.

then everything goes to the server in ONE request

the framework's reload chatter is not written, everything else is

a second install does nothing (a hot reload cannot double the lines)
only real entries are kept, and cut to size
a body that is not an entry list gives nothing
one line per entry: time, level, page, message; more lines indented
